meta.description:
The items below are mandatory and will be briefed to all personnel. Develop a work center specific JSTG based on Attachment 4, Job Safety Training Outline (JSTO), on safety, fire protection/prevention and health requirements. Documents will be maintained and centrally located, readily available to supervisor and individual. The 14 mandatory items below can be documented as one item, i.e., course code for JSTO mandatory training. Job specific items and any additional training identified in a Bioenvironmental survey will be documented individually, as appropriate.  The supervisor will document and maintain completed training in the work area.  
Methods of documentation may include, but are not limited to, the AF IMT 55, Employee Safety and Health Record, electronic mediums such as AFFORMs/MAF LOG C2/G081 or locally developed products. If the AF IMT 55 is mandated for use as the training documentation device, the entity that mandated the form usage will prescribe the requirement in writing to include entries that require signatures, e.g., HAZCOM, respirator, powered industrial trucks, lockout/tagout, fall protection, confined spaces, radiation safety, laser safety, etc. Note:  Training requirements vary, i.e., some documents may require the signature of the supervisor or the person who conducted the training, while other documents may require the initials of the individual (trainee) and trainer/supervisor. 
Documentation will contain the following minimum data: trainee name (last, first, middle initial), type of training and date of training. Neither the trainer or trainee signature is required unless specified in writing by the applicable chain of authority. Note:  If the Integrated Maintenance Data System (IMDS), Core Automated Maintenance System (CAMS), etc., cannot support minimum documentation requirements, then they are not suitable as a documentation product.

meta.medicalFacility:
During normal duty hours on weekdays, personnel are to report to Dover AFB Clinic for assessment and treatment of injuries suffered while on-the-job. Civilian employees may elect to receive treatment from their personal physician.

If the injury or medical condition does not permit the injured person to first report to Dover AFB Clinic, the individuals should be treated at the closest medical facility which in most cases will be Bay Health Medical Center (otherwise known as Kent General Hospital) located in downtown Dover, contact information is: (302) 674-4700.

The Base Clinic is located in Building 300. Also, advise member that the Base Clinic no longer provides 24 hour emergency service. Make sure the individual understands the procedure to get medical attention on and off duty as per TRICARE provider procedures (1-877-TRICARE or 1-877-874-2273).

meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
Requirements of Air Force Traffic Safety Program, including mandatory use of seat belts and helmets, speed limits, local traffic hazards, and personal risk management.  Additionally, brief use of seat belts and helmets, speed limits, local traffic hazards, and personal RM.  Additionally, brief uee of electronic devides while GMV/PMV on or off base. IAW AFI  91-207.  If Applicable, discuss Motorcycle Safety Training Requirements Before Riding A Motorcycle. (AFI 91-202 para. A4.1.9)

Seat belts will be worn on and off-base any time a vehicle is in motion. Emphasize that wear is MANDATORY. Discuss possible administrative actions if caught without utilizing the seat belt (i.e. possibility of losing driving privileges, tickets, fines, etc.).  Discuss flightline- required usage in forward facing seats. Remember that use of belts is mandatory on or off base, on or off duty to include back seats. You will get ticketed. Buckle Up! (Ref AFI 91-207)

NOTE:  Placing the shoulder strap under the arm or not using/disconnecting automatic belts constitutes “improper use” and could result in a citation - or worse yet additional/more severe injuries should you get into an accident.

If you are required to drive on the flightline, you must accomplish flightline driver training. Completion of the course includes formal training, a written exam, airfield diagram test, both a day and night familiarization, and a practical evaluation if required. 

Cell phone use while driving is prohibited.  If you are driving and you need to take a call, use hands free device or safely pull off to the side of the road, put your hazards lights on and take the call. 

Be aware of severely congested traffic on Highway 13 and Route 1 in Dover during NASCAR weekend. Use defensive driving techniques.  Attempt to accomplish errands during the races, not before or after.

selectedModules.title: Hazardous Energy Control
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 21; 29 CFR 1910.147 - The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train authorized employees to recognize hazardous energy sources, the type and magnitude of energy present, and the methods and means for isolation and control. Train affected employees on the purpose and use of lockout/tagout procedures, and instruct all other employees on the prohibition against restarting locked or tagged equipment.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Document initial and refresher training when job assignments, machines, processes, or energy control procedures change, or when inspections show employee knowledge gaps.
selectedModules.link: S:\CEO\CEOIH - Copy\04. Safety\7. TAB G - JSTG and Training Material\Training Material

selectedModules.title: Fall Arrest Systems
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 13; 29 CFR 1910.66 - Powered platforms for building maintenance; 29 CFR 1926.503 - Training requirements
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train employees exposed to fall hazards to recognize fall hazards and the procedures to minimize them, including use and inspection of fall arrest systems.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Cover anchorage selection, rescue planning, and equipment inspections before personnel use personal fall arrest systems in assigned tasks.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Walking-Working Surfaces and Fall Protection
selectedModules.link: S:\CEO\CEOIH - Copy\04. Safety\7. TAB G - JSTG and Training Material\Training Material

selectedModules.title: Hazard Communication
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on hazardous chemicals in their work area, labeling systems, safety data sheets, and the measures they can take to protect themselves during normal operations and foreseeable emergencies.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide HazCom training upon initial assignment, whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced, and when new tasks expose workers to different hazardous materials. Ensure workers know how to access local SDS information and labeling guidance.
